Car-free field guide

Shoreline Gateway, Long Beach

777 E Ocean Blvd, Long Beach, CA 90802Unit 2607, 26th floor, plan A7Northwest corner of Ocean Blvd & Alamitos Ave

Everything below is measured on foot from the lobby door. The East Village Arts District starts one block north, the sand is across Ocean Blvd, and the Metro A Line is about a 12 minute walk west. You can live here without a car for the first few months.

Getting around without a car

Load a TAP card once. It works on Metro rail, LA Metro buses and Long Beach Transit buses. Fares below are the standard adult fare and the two free shuttles need no card at all.

Rail

Metro A Line

$1.75 per ride, 2 hour free transfers on TAP.

Board at 1st Street Station (1st & Pine, ~12 min walk) or at the Downtown Long Beach terminus (1st & Pacific). Roughly an hour to 7th St/Metro Center in DTLA and a bit more to Union Station. Runs late and frequently.

Timetables

Bus

Long Beach Transit

$1.25 per ride, cash or TAP. 30 day passes available.

Route 121 runs along Ocean Blvd right past the building, east to Belmont Shore and Cal State Long Beach and west into Downtown. Several more routes run on Broadway and 3rd St a block north. The Transit Mall on 1st St connects to nearly every route in the system.

Routes and the LBT app

Free shuttle

LBT Passport

Free, Friday to Sunday, about every 15 min, roughly 10am to 8pm.

Loops Downtown: Pine Ave, Shoreline Village, the Aquarium, the Convention Center and the Queen Mary. Handy for the waterfront on weekends.

Verify days and hours Sources disagree on whether it also runs weekdays.

Free on-demand

LB Circuit

Free, request in the Ride Circuit app.

Electric shuttles covering Downtown, Alamitos Beach and east to Alamitos Bay and Belmont Shore, plus the Queen Mary. Generally Thursday through Sunday afternoons and evenings. Think of it as free rideshare for dinner in Belmont Shore.

Service area and hours

Bike

Long Beach Bike Share

Run by Pedal Movement. Pay as you go, monthly or annual plans. Bike Share For All gives eligible residents, students and workers an annual membership for $5.

The Shoreline Pedestrian Bikepath runs on the sand below the building from Shoreline Village to Belmont Shore, so a bike gets you to the Pike, the marina and 2nd St without touching a road.

Plans · Bike Share For All

Airport

Long Beach Airport (LGB)

About 6 miles north. Long Beach Transit routes 104 and 111 serve the airport; rideshare from the building is usually 15 to 20 minutes.

Verify route Check the LBT trip planner for the current airport connection from Downtown.

  • Groceries without a car: Vons is a 6 minute walk and delivers. For a bigger haul, Smart & Final on Atlantic is one bus ride, and Whole Foods and Trader Joe's are out on PCH, best done by bus 121 plus a short walk or by rideshare.
  • Nights out: Pine Ave and the Promenade are a 15 minute walk, and the A Line runs late. 2nd St in Belmont Shore is a 10 minute bus or a free Circuit ride.
  • Beach days: Alamitos Beach is directly across Ocean Blvd. Take the stairs or ramp down the bluff at Alamitos Ave.

    Unit 2607: floor plan and room sizes

    Plan A7, which the architect's set labels unit 1C-3. One bedroom plus a den, one bath, a 14 foot balcony off the bedroom, and a curved window wall across the whole living room. The listed 1,010 sq ft is the marketing figure. Measured to the inside face of the walls the floor area is about 950 sq ft, which is normal for how buildings quote size.

    How these numbers were made

    Nobody publishes room dimensions for this building. The sizes above come from the building's own unit-map drawing of plan A7 (a 4,958 px architectural plan), scaled against the listed 1,010 sq ft and checked against fixtures of known size. The check landed within a few percent on four independent items: the doors measure 36", the kitchen counter 25½" deep, the island 6'×3', and the tub about 5'. Treat each figure as ±3%, or about ±4" on a 12 foot wall. Before buying anything that has to fit tightly, confirm on move-in day with a tape, or ask leasing for the dimensioned A7 plan from the construction set.

    • Sign the lease in the resident portal within three days of the email.
    • Reserve an elevator slot for move-in day. Only two reservations per day, so book early and ask whether furniture deliveries need their own slot. Give Caravana (or any delivery crew) the slot time and the elevator and door dimensions above.
    • Cashier's check for $5,791.12 made out to "Shoreline Gateway". After move-in, rent runs through Bilt (paywithbilt.com), which also pays with a bank account or card.
    • Renters insurance with $300,000 liability, in place at least 48 hours before January 7, every adult occupant on the policy, and "Shoreline Gateway, PO Box 100513, Florence, SC 29502" listed as additional insured. Your own insurer or Assurant, (800) 432-8612.
    • Electricity: open a Southern California Edison account, (800) 655-4555 or sce.com, and give the office the full account number. Gas, water, trash, sewer and pest control come on the monthly Conservice bill.
    • Internet: 500/500 Mbps and a router are inside the $95 monthly technology fee, but you must activate it. Call Frontier's bulk line at (844) 660-0648, option 2, say the HOA is Shoreline Gateway, and give the unit as "2607" at 777 E. Ocean Blvd (not "Apt").

    Measure on day one

    • Bedroom head wall (expect about 13'3") and the clear width at the foot of the bed.
    • Den long wall (expect 12'0") and depth at the door side (expect about 6'2").
    • Distance from the island's living side to the glass (expect about 17'6") for sofa and rug sizing.
    • Ceiling height and window sill height. Neither is on the plan.
    • The turn from the entry into the living room: the front door is 34" wide and the entry is 5'2" × 4'0", so check the swing room for an 88" headboard.
    • Balcony door swing and railing height.

    3D walkthroughs of several plans are on the building's virtual tours page. The tours are not labeled by plan name, so look for the one with a den and a curved living room wall. For your own furniture, open the 3D planner tab.

    Room planner for 2607

    Drag furniture around the measured plan. Walls, glass and the balcony are built from the same drawing as the dimensions above, so a red item is one that overlaps a wall or sits off the floor. Rotate with the 90° and 5° buttons, or press "Den wall" to set a piece flush against the angled den wall; remove with the X; add anything you are considering with its real width, depth and height in inches. Your layout stays in this browser. Use Copy to hand the layout to Claude or to another device.

    Den as office: the suggested layout puts a 72" standing desk against the bedroom wall at the window end of the den, chair in front, with about 4½ feet behind it and 3 feet to the glass. The wall is a clear 12 feet, so up to an 8 foot desk fits. Two 27" monitors on arms and a 4-slot laptop stand fit on that top. Daylight comes from the right, which keeps it off the screens. Two more den layouts are one click away: "L-desk in the den" places the FlexiSpot E7L (76" run plus a 55" × 28" return toward the glass for the laptops), and "Desk facing the glass" turns the desk to the view, which puts the monitors in front of a bright east window; that one is there for comparison, not as a recommendation.

    The Jessica king (88" × 88¾" × 43¼") fits in the bedroom with the headboard on the top wall. The plan shows a 4 foot wide, 6 inch deep bump on that wall on the window side, probably a chase, so the headboard sits about 6" off the wall. Pushed toward the window side, the bed leaves about 4'0" on the closet side so the closet door clears, about 3'4" at the foot to the den wall, and a wedge on the window side that narrows from roughly 23" at the head to a few inches at the foot because that wall angles in. An 18" nightstand fits on the window side. On the closet side a nightstand would sit inside the closet door swing, so plan on a wall shelf or a very narrow table there. It is a wide platform: the mattress is 76", the frame adds 6" each side.

    Top view. Drag to move. Dark bands are walls, light blue is glass. The balcony is top right.

    3D view. Drag to orbit, scroll or pinch to zoom, right-drag to pan. Walls are cut at 3 ft so you can see in. Floors show wood in the living areas, carpet in the bedroom and tile in the bath as the building renders them; confirm finishes with leasing.

      Den office: chair, standing desk, monitors

      The den is 12 feet wide along the bedroom wall and 6 to 8½ feet deep, with the door at the left end and glass on the right. The desk goes against the bedroom wall at the window end, so you face the wall with daylight from the right and the door behind your left shoulder. The back wall is a clear 12 feet (the den door is on the side wall), so an 8 foot desk fits with room to spare and a 72" or 80" is comfortable. The planner's suggested layout now uses a 72 × 30.

      Catan plan

      The round 35" Modus Oskar lift-top in the living room is the Catan table: the base-game hex board is about 22" across and sits on it with room for cards and the robber, the top lifts to 28" so nobody hunches, and the box, expansions and dice live in the storage well under the top, so the game is always where you play it. For five or six players, or Seafarers, the 48" round dining table by the south window takes the bigger layout. If you want it on display, a 22" square hex frame holds the board set up and hangs on the short wall under the bathroom block between games; that is a DIY frame or an Etsy buy and I have not priced one.
